procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (must be outside a free zone, with a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form with HS code, description, quantity and value; upload proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online; the fee ranges from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on invoice value.
Submit the application; processing takes about one working day.
Receive the approved certificate, or a return with comments to correct.
The certificate is valid for 12 months from issue, covers one import, and must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing.
Keep origin records, including cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is confirmed only in secondary sources.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only, not the CEPA product-specific rule test.
